pageCache.text:
Seeing Possibilities
Realising Dreams
Welcome to Willow Dene
Willow Dene is an outstanding special school for children of primary and secondary age, and young people of sixth form age. We are based over two beautiful sites in the Plumstead area. We are a values-based learning community completely focused on building provision around the needs of each child or young person and their families. We are a very happy community and aim to offer our families support to enable children to thrive, and enjoy living and learning.
Willow Dene is the only special school in Greenwich which meets the needs of children and young people aged 2-19. Our children and young people have a wide range of special educational needs. Our teachers are exceptional practitioners, who work as part of an extensive multi-disciplinary team of specialists to plan learning pathways, that ensure children and young people are given the best opportunities to thrive and become independent.
We are part of Compass Eko Trust, a charitable trust of 28 schools that work as one to achieve the very best for all children and all communities.
We are proud to be part of the Compass Eko team who were awarded TES Inclusive Trust of the Year 2025-26.

pageCache.text:
Aims, Values & Ethos
Willow Dene is a confident and successful school. At the centre of its vision is the understanding that ‘exceptional learners need exceptional teachers’ and this drives everything we do. As the result of a passionate and consistent focus on the quality of pedagogy and personalised curriculum, the school is an innovator of practice and provision. We now support other settings in developing the quality of their own practice and will be integral to national developments in the provision for children with special educational needs. Willow Dene is an ambitious, forward thinking and fully inclusive community that is very successful at removing barriers to access and learning for all its children and families.
Our school values are enshrined in the provision at Willow Dene and underpin all that we do:

pageCache.pageTitle: Willow Dene School - Welcome from our Head Teacher
pageCache.text:
Welcome from our Head Teacher
It is my pleasure to welcome you to Willow Dene.
Willow Dene is an outstanding special school for children and young people with a range of Special Educational Needs aged 2-19, primarily from the Royal Borough of Greenwich. Since 2011, we have been constantly growing and evolving to better meet the needs of our children, young people and their families, and the most recent part of our journey been the addition of sixth form which opened in September 2023. Willow Dene consists of Toucan Specialist Provision for 2 Year Olds, Willow Dene Swingate Lane for our primary aged children, Willow Dene Oakmere Road for our secondary aged children and Willow Dene Sixth Form, based in our new building at Oakmere Road, for our young people. We are lucky to be located near to leafy green spaces and at the heart of our local communities.
We are very happy and proud that Ofsted have recognised the achievements of our children, the dedication and skill of our staff team and the ethos of support and teamwork within our school.
Our Ofsted report from the November 2022 visit says that:
"Pupils thrive and excel at this exceptional school. Leaders and staff have very high expectations for all pupils. They work hard to make sure that learning is fun and that lessons capture the interests of pupils."
We are looking forward to continuing to grow and develop together to positively affect the futures of children with special educational needs at Willow Dene and beyond.
We are delighted to be working with the wider Compass team on the plans for Rowan Wood, our new Compass Special Free School. Rowan Wood secondary school opened in September 2025, offering children and young people and the team the unique opportunity to learn from Willow Dene through co-location for the 25/26 academic year. Rowan Wood secondary school building opened in September 2026 and we are currently planning for the primary school.
We aim to provide the highest possible quality of education for our children and young people. This begins with the positive relationships that all our staff team build with children, young people and families. We know that our children and young people learn best when they are happy and settled in school. We constantly talk to our parents and families so that they are fully included in their child or young person's school experience. Our highly skilled teachers and support staff ensure that our child-centred provision considers every aspect of the child or young person's day. Our curriculum, bespoke assessment and well-matched resourcing are all designed specifically for our children, making sure that we are always aspirational for their learning and futures.
We are always moving forward, seeking new ways to develop what we do. At Willow Dene, research and innovation are always evident. This is supported by high quality collaborative working within school and beyond. Our relationships with therapists and other health professionals, national organisations and many others is one of mutual support and benefit to our children and young people. We are a MOVE Centre of Excellence and a National Autistic Society Accredited setting with Advanced Status.
We are committed to supporting children and young people with complex needs outside of Willow Dene. We have a well embedded SEND hub and inclusion support offer which ensures high quality inclusion across Compass Eko schools and the Royal Borough of Greenwich. We were delighted to be awarded TES Inclusive Trust of the Year 2026.
Our school was designed with our children and young people in mind. You will see this from the buildings themselves, specialist learning environments such as our swimming pool and sensory garden, the way that classrooms are furnished and resourced and how we meet the needs of individuals, with specialist equipment.
We aim for all our children and young people to become valued and valuable members of society. We are constantly looking for engaging, rich opportunities within our local community and beyond so that all children and young people have experiences which link them to their wider world. In 26/27 we will be working alongside Royal Borough of Greenwich to implement an exciting Post-19 pilot project, supporting more of our young people leaving school to have a high quality and purposeful adult life.
We are very proud of our school. Willow Dene is an exciting place to be and we hope you get a sense of this from our website. We recommend looking at our Willow Dene Tours, Documentary, and Instagram feeds. Our doors are always open, both to parents and professionals. We enjoy sharing what we do. Please do visit in person if you would like to know more.
Rachel Harrison Executive Head Teacher

Ofsted & Challenge Partners
Ofsted
Willow Dene was inspected by Ofsted in November 2022. We were delighted and proud to have been graded 'Outstanding', in a report that recognises the strength and dedication of the whole team at Willow Dene and the ‘exceptional’ provision we offer for children and families.
Ofsted Report Quotes - November 2022
Pupils thrive and excel at this exceptional school. Leaders and staff have very high expectations for all pupils. They work hard to make sure that learning is fun and that lessons capture the interests of pupils.
Behaviour at the school is exemplary. It is a calm and orderly environment for everyone.
Leaders know their pupils well. They have ensured that the curriculum is ambitious and specialised. The expertise of therapists is woven through the school day.
People show how much they like coming to school in the happy way that they arrive in the morning. Relationships between adults and pupils are a strength of the school.

Challenge Partners
What is Challenge Partners?
The Challenge Partners multi-academy Trust Peer Review (TPR) enables development and improvement in host Trusts through challenge and collaboration. It provides reviewers with unique insights to support their own Trust’s development, and helps share knowledge about what works across the education system so all can benefit.
The Trust Peer Review:
Evaluates the Trust on its own terms
Captures and shares effective practice
Identifies areas for improvement
Is expert-facilitated
How it works
Led by an independent expert over three-days, the external review team works with host Trust leaders to build a picture of how school improvement operates across the trust and the impact it is having. This informs professional dialogue about strengths, areas for development and next steps, which are captured in a written report. There is also the opportunity for the host Trust to harness the expertise of their peers to explore a particular challenge they are facing and identify ways forward.
The Trust Peer Review relies on asking powerful, open questions in a spirit of appreciative inquiry and collaboration. We know all Trusts are different and that there is not a single formula for Trust success, so our reviews do not start with a framework or checklist, or otherwise presume to know “the answer”. The review does not check compliance or provide an audit of finance, governance or HR – though we do consider how these important factors contribute to school improvement.

School visit June 2026
We really enjoyed seeing the school and hearing from you about the amazing work you and your teams are doing for the children and young people. It was so clear the journey the school(s) have been on and the passion all staff have.
It was good to hear about the different elements and workstreams and how they really make a difference for children and young people. I found the physical development work and the health benefits particularly inspiring. We could really see the teamwork and commitment across staff as we went around the schools and the positive atmosphere was clear. Please thank your teams again and best wishes for this last term!
Little Wandle Live Event – June 2026
Thank you so much for opening your virtual doors and letting us see a glimpse of Willow Dene. Your enthusiasm and passion for giving all children the best chance was infectious. Thank you so much to all of the amazing staff and wonderful children that were involved.
Thank you, I found today's session extremely useful and helpful for getting started. It was really helpful having the time to ask questions after each section in the break out rooms.

My daughter absolutely loved it, thank you to everyone who made it happen. It was an amazing event.

It was a pleasure to work with you and the team for your consultancy visit last week...Please pass on my thanks to everyone, if their cocktail of passion and professionalism could be bottled - not WD40 but WDPP - I'd buy it!

Thank you so much for today, the kids loved it. They had an amazing time and went to bed early because of the excitement from today.

Thank you so much for inviting us to visit your wonderful school last week. We were incredibly grateful that you gave up so much of your time to show us the systems and processes you have developed, and to share the ethos behind everything you have created at Willow Dene.
Walking around the school, it was very clear to see the impact you have had on the provision for the children in your care. What you have built is really impressive, and it was so insightful for us to learn more about your approach. We are very inspired!!
Thank you to you both, and your team for making us feel so welcome! You have an amazing school and I came away with lots of ideas!

Thank you for the incredibly insightful and uplifting visit to Willow Dene, it was brilliant to see your schools in action. We were particularly impressed by the outstanding quality of the provision, not only in terms of the resources and environment – which were well-ordered, vibrant, clean and engaging – but most importantly, the calibre of the adults working with the children.

Amazing experience! Thank you Mark for showing us the school!
Thank you Mark for the tour, such a wonderful school. Lovely and calm.
Big thanks for the tour, such a great space for the children to come to.
Little Wandle Live Event March 2025
Thank you for a great day! It was great to see such an amazing SEND provision! Today has helped me think of which direction I need to go in with Little Wandle!
Thank you so much for such an inspiring day! It was a pleasure to have a tour of Willow Dene and see the outstanding provision for the children and young people in your care. Your knowledge and expertise is exemplary! Thank you.
Thank you so much to Claire, Kelly and your fabulous team for one warm welcome. Your school is an absolute joy to spend time in and one children are so lucky to be in such exceptional hands. Everyone has got so much out of our time here today.

pageCache.pageTitle: Willow Dene School - The Willow Dene Curriculum
pageCache.text:
The Willow Dene Curriculum
The Willow Dene Curriculum
At Willow Dene, we believe that every CYP is unique and deserves a curriculum that recognises and celebrates their individual strengths, interests, needs and aspirations. Our curriculum is ambitious, personalised and meaningful, providing opportunities for all CYP to develop the knowledge, skills, independence and confidence they need to thrive in school and beyond. Our intent is to enable all CYP to become active learners, moving towards greater independence, autonomy, control and choice, whilst developing the communication skills needed to express their needs, wants, thoughts and opinions.
The Curriculum Offer outlines how we provide teaching and learning opportunities that are essential to the learning and development of every CYP. Our curriculum is based on the National Curriculum programmes of study for Key Stages 1 to 4 and includes all statutory curriculum requirements. In Key Stage 5, the curriculum is personalised around Preparation for Adulthood outcomes, Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) targets and the individual aspirations of each learner. The curriculum is carefully designed to meet the diverse needs of our school community, reflects our key values and complies with the duties of the Equality Act 2010 and the SEND Code of Practice 2014.
We place a strong emphasis on meaningful learning experiences. Our curriculum maximises cross-curricular links, provides opportunities to practise and generalise skills across different contexts, and uses a text-led approach to enrich learning wherever appropriate. Central to this is our Learner-Centred Pedagogy, which underpins every aspect of teaching and learning and ensures that every CYP can access a curriculum that is engaging, relevant and aspirational.
Learner-Centred Pedagogy
Our learner-centred pedagogy places every CYP and their family at the heart of everything we do. We recognise that no two learners are the same, so our teaching is responsive, flexible and carefully adapted to meet individual strengths, needs and starting points. Through nurturing relationships, thoughtfully designed environments and personalised teaching approaches, we create learning experiences that support regulation, build confidence and enable meaningful progress.
We believe that successful learning happens when CYP feel safe, valued, understood and ready to engage. Our learner-centred pedagogy is built around four interconnected elements that work together to create the best possible outcomes for every learner.
Positive and consistent relationships form the foundation of learning at Willow Dene. Our staff develop trusting and meaningful relationships with CYP, helping them feel emotionally safe, supported and confident. Through responsive and attuned interactions, adults provide encouragement, reassurance and co-regulation, enabling learners to develop resilience, self-confidence and a strong sense of belonging within the school community. These relationships create the security that allows CYP to engage fully in learning and develop their independence over time.
Enabling Environments
Our learning environments are intentionally designed to meet the diverse needs of our CYP. Spaces are organised, predictable and responsive, helping learners understand expectations, make choices and develop increasing independence. Through the use of visual supports, structured routines, sensory considerations and engaging learning opportunities, we create environments where CYP feel safe to explore, communicate, problem solve and succeed. By removing barriers and promoting accessibility, our environments support every learner to participate meaningfully in school life.
We know that effective teaching is not about one approach, but about selecting the right strategy at the right time. Our teaching toolkit consists of a wide range of evidence-informed approaches that support learning across the curriculum. These include facilitating learning, scaffolding, modelling, chunking learning into manageable steps, embedding learning through play and using visual supports to enhance understanding and independence. Staff carefully select and adapt these approaches to ensure learning remains accessible, motivating and appropriately challenging for every CYP.
We understand that learning can only flourish when CYP feel safe, regulated and emotionally supported. Readiness to learn is therefore a fundamental aspect of our curriculum. By prioritising emotional well-being, communication, positive relationships and regulation, we support CYP to become more open to exploration, engagement and new learning opportunities. When learners are ready to learn, they are better able to acquire knowledge, develop skills, build independence and achieve their individual goals.
We have a carefully considered and sequenced approach to early reading which ensures that every learner develops the foundations they need to become successful readers.
For CYP working at an Early Development level, we focus on building the essential pre-reading skills that underpin future success. These include early visual, auditory and motor skills, attention and listening skills, early communication and interaction skills, as well as memory and sequencing abilities.
For CYP working at an Emergent Concept level, we establish the foundations for reading through a strong focus on language comprehension and word recognition. Learners develop vocabulary, language structures, phonological awareness and background knowledge through high-quality stories, poems, rhymes and listening activities. These experiences help children build the language skills that are fundamental to future reading success.
For CYP working at Basic Concept and Applying Knowledge levels, who have secured the necessary foundations, we support them in becoming effective early readers. We continue to develop language comprehension alongside more formal decoding and word recognition skills. We use the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds systematic synthetic phonics programme to build learners' understanding of the alphabetic code, enabling them to master phonics for reading and spelling. Alongside this, learners access carefully matched Big Cat decodable books, allowing them to apply their phonics knowledge while developing fluency, confidence and enjoyment in reading.
Through this progressive approach, we aim to foster a lifelong love of reading and ensure that all CYP can access high-quality texts and meaningful literacy experiences.
Teaching of Religious Education (RE)
RE is not taught as a stand-alone subject at Willow Dene, elements of the RE curriculum feature in strands of Time, People, Place and Culture (TPPC). These include strands of 'Community' and 'Cultures' which will contain reference to a range of world religions, cultures, world and religious rituals, festivals and celebrations. Whilst we do not teach about the content of religious teachings in depth, we do aim to teach children about diversity, respect and tolerance of other religious beliefs. TPPC is taught through storytelling, use of props, artefacts, sensory and immersive experiences. Parents and carers have the right to withdraw their children from sessions that link to RE. Please inform your child's class teacher if you do not wish for your child to partake in these elements of the TPPC curriculum.
Bringing Our Curriculum to Life
Our curriculum and learner-centred pedagogy work seamlessly together. Responsive adults, enabling environments, effective teaching strategies and readiness to learn provide the foundation upon which all curriculum experiences are built. This ensures that every CYP can access learning in a way that is meaningful, personalised and ambitious.
By placing the learner at the centre of every decision, we empower CYP to become confident communicators, curious explorers, resilient learners and active members of their community. Our curriculum is designed not only to develop knowledge and skills but also to promote well-being, independence, choice and self-determination.
At Willow Dene, we are committed to ensuring that every CYP is supported to flourish, achieve and reach their fullest potential through a curriculum that is engaging, relevant and truly learner centred.
To find out more about our curriculum coverage and specific information such as the sixth form curriculum, refer to 'In This Section'.

Communication & Letters Home
At Willow Dene every child from Early Years to Key Stage 4. has a home school contact book which helps to provide a direct exchange of information and dialogue between home and school. We aim to ensure that parents and carers are fully informed about their child’s daily activities and wellbeing, as well as providing our children with a voice to enable them to communicate their daily activities at home or school. We believe that all children will learn better if home, and school, work together in partnership. To achieve this aim, we ask parents / carers to support and sign our home school agreement.
Every young person in sixth form has their own Ipad, with the EFL app downloaded onto it, which replaces the home school contact books. These are used by adults and young people to take photos and videos of their daily activities and achievements. Young people take their IPads home so photos can be taken and shared between home and school. Staff and parents or carers communicate through the EFL app to ensure they are fully informed about their young person's day. To achieve this aim, we ask parents or carers to complete our Ipad communication agreement.
We use the EfL Family app to enable us to digitally share photos, videos and messages between home and school. This allows class teams and families to share celebrations of children’s successes and build connections. We know that close partnerships between school and home lead to better outcomes for children. Providing effective means to share ways of working and progress supports this process. The app also enables meaningful connections between the wider network of people who are important in the child’s life by allowing families to share things we are all proud of more easily and securely.
We have one formal parents' evening in the autumn term, and an informal parents’ evening at the end of the year to recognise and celebrate children’s progress. Parents’ evenings are an opportunity to talk about your child, including how they have settled into class and to discuss their learning. Teachers share ways in which your child is learning and making progress through photos, videos and discussion. This provides parents with the opportunity to see the specialist approaches, equipment and resources your child uses in action.
Annual reviews are held once a year to review children’s learning and progress. Class teachers will provide a report of the progress children have made in all aspects of their learning. Children are encouraged to be a key part of this process and a video demonstrating their achievements, likes and progress will be shown. New areas for learning and achievement are discussed and objectives are set in collaboration with parents to plan for their child’s future.
The Compass Partnership of Schools is pleased to announce that we have partnered with Bromcom to run our schools’ management information systems. This has enabled us to deploy the MyChildAtSchool [MCAS] online portal, enabling you to communicate with your child’s school via a web browser.
MyChildAtSchool provides:
• Communication facilities to improve contact between parents and schools
• Option to purchase school dinners, join clubs or book trips

Governance
Each Compass school has a local school committee composed of a group of volunteers drawn from the community, each bringing a range of skills, expertise and professional experience. Our Governors provide essential links between the school, parents/carers and the local community. Governors work with staff and parents in an atmosphere of co-operation to provide the best possible framework for educating our children. They are involved in all aspects of school life and meet regularly with leadership teams.
Governors fulfil their responsibilities by:
Supporting the school and its ambition by working strategically to develop and implement vision and ethos;
Ensuring that the children are receiving the best education and achieve the best outcomes by monitoring the quality of teaching and standards across the school;
Making sure the school uses its financial resources effectively and in line with the budget plan;
Accounting to all stakeholders for the school’s performance and for the decisions they make.
If you are interested in becoming a Governor at our school or would like to hear more about what the role involves, please email contact@compassps.uk
Chair of Governors – Lynne Wainwright
Lynne is the Chair of Governors for Willow Dene School. She has been a governor since November 2018. She is a lecturer in children’s nursing at King’s College London, having worked for over 25 years as a children’s / neonatal intensive care nurse.
Lynne has 30 years experience as a school governor in a variety of settings and is passionate about ensuring that all children receive the best education and care.
Lynne can be contacted at the Willow Dene School Contact address.

Link governors should focus on a specific aspect of school life and report back to the Local School Committee on it. Their job is to raise the profile of the issue, monitor it, and provide support and challenge to key school staff.
At Willow Dene and Rowan Wood all members of the Local School committee have specific areas that they link with –
Pupil Premium, Sports Premium and Free School Meals
Kafayet Eletu and Nicole Allwood
Safeguarding, CLA, Prevent and attendance, SEND, Governor training and development, Allergies
Safeguarding and Health and safety are monitored on a termly basis with a report to the next committee meeting.
Link governors for other areas will liaise with the staff lead to make prearranged visits to school with a clear focus. These visits will then be reported back to the LSC and aspects discussed as necessary with senior leaders.
All governors are involved in termly monitoring mornings linked to the schools’ core priorities at which we receive information regarding the priority as well as undertake visits to areas of the school to see how things are being implemented and the impact of these on children and young people and staff.
